instruction: I want to buy everything in my amazon cart. I have a promo code applied to the cart, but today I received a new promotional email from Amazon. See if it is a better deal. Place an order for my home delivery with whichever option is cheaper.
notes: Two apps (amazon, gmail) plus supervisor. The price comparison cannot be computed in STRIPS, so it is modeled as knowledge flow: show_cart with the current code records its discount; the email code is learned from gmail.show_thread; applying the email code requires the discount of the code being replaced to be known (found-cart-discount ?prev); a second show_cart with the email code applied reveals the runtime-selected object promo-best (static cart-reveals relation), which is then applied before placing the order. If promo-best resolves to promo-new at runtime the second apply is redundant and can be skipped; if amazon rejects applying over an existing code, call amazon.remove_promo_code_from_cart first (not modeled). place_order requires a known home address id (name == home), a known payment card id and the best code applied; no gift wrapping is ever added and no address is modified, matching the evaluation. The task asks no question, so complete_task carries no answer; its record parameters only tie its precondition to the goal literals.
